finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar forwards an attacker-supplied URL to axios.get server-side. The only check is that the value is a string starting with https://, which restricts the scheme but not the host, IP, or port, so internal or link-local targets are reachable.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10), unauthenticated JSON body of POST /profile/avatar

trace.note: POST /profile/avatar route handler receives req via express.json()
url = req.body.avatarUrl, taken without further processing
typeof string and startsWith("https://") checks only; host, IP, and port are unrestricted
axios.get(url) issues a server-side GET to the attacker-chosen URL; axios follows redirects by default (not verified in this environment)
Only img.data.length is returned, so the response body is not echoed; attacker learns length and timing only

finding.guards_checked: server.js:11 typeof string check: blocks non-string input, does not restrict destination. server.js:11 startsWith("https://"): restricts scheme only; https://169.254.169.254, https://10.x.x.x, https://localhost:port, and https://users.internal:8080 all pass. No hostname allowlist, DNS/IP range filtering, port restriction, maxRedirects:0, redirect re-validation, timeout, or maxContentLength.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 only checks typeof string and startsWith("https://"), which is a scheme-only check. No hostname or IP allowlist, port restriction, maxRedirects, or timeout exists on the path. There is no authentication middleware on the route (server.js:9-16, express.json() at server.js:5 only parses the body).
verdict.reason: The value comes from the unauthenticated body at server.js:10 and reaches axios.get at server.js:14 after only a scheme check at server.js:11, so an attacker can send https://169.254.169.254/ or an internal host, making this a blind SSRF whose effect is limited to the returned byte length (server.js:15). The trace is accurate; the claim that redirects are followed is unverified here but does not affect the verdict.
